title: This voice isn't real. My laptop made it.
caption: Local voice cloning: an 8 s public-domain clip in, 21 s of speech out in 32 s, $0, no API key. Open code (MIT), open weights (Apache 2.0). Could you tell? Comment the second it sounded fake.
credits: Voice: Steve Jackson, LibriVox (CC0), via voice-zero
Model: VoxCPM2 (OpenBMB), MLX port by mlx-community

engagement.prompt: Could you tell it was fake? Comment the second you knew.
engagement.pinned_comment: Where did it sound fake to you? Give me the timestamp. The voice is a public-domain LibriVox sample; the code and weights are open.

scenes.narration: This voice isn't real. My laptop made it.
All it heard was eight seconds of a public domain voice. Now it says anything I type.
Real run. Twenty one seconds of speech, in thirty two seconds, on a MacBook. Zero dollars.
Fact: it runs locally, for free, on open code and open weights. How does it compare to ElevenLabs? I haven't tested that.
Could you tell it was fake? Comment the second you knew. The code is on GitHub.
